statement: The held-out split is defined by the stream seed below. The transition table that defines the language is public and lives on the agent surface, because an agent that cannot see the language it optimises against is not solving an optimization task. The tokens the graded loss is computed on are drawn from a stream this seed alone generates, so they are the same distribution and never the same tokens the agent container trains on. Harbor assembles the agent surface out of task.toml, instruction.md and environment/ only, so this file is absent from it by construction rather than by a filter.
disjointness: The train stream seed bound in environment/operating_point.json is 20260619 and this seed is 907741. Two numpy PCG64 streams seeded differently are independent, so no held-out token position is a train token position.
